tools.name: generate_leads
tools.title: Generate Leads
tools.description:
[BETA] Find B2B professionals by role, industry, company size, and location. Returns PEOPLE + COMPANIES + VERIFIED EMAILS in one run. 1 credit per verified lead returned.

⚡ SMART ROUTING — IMPORTANT: When a user asks to "find people", "find companies", or "find leads", choose the included discovery lane unless they explicitly need verified emails:

OPTION A — Lead Generation (generate_leads): 1 credit/row
  ✅ Returns people WITH verified emails + company data
  ✅ Best when the user needs contact-ready leads for outreach
  ✅ Includes deduplication and email verification

OPTION B — Find People (find_people_signaliz) or Find Companies (find_companies_signaliz): included standard discovery
  ✅ No Signaliz fresh enrichment credits for standard people/company discovery
  ✅ Best when the user just needs names/titles/companies (no verified emails needed)
  ❌ Does NOT include verified emails

Ask the user: "I can run this two ways:
1. **Lead Generation** (1 credit/row) — returns people + companies + verified emails, ready for outreach
2. **Find People / Find Companies** (included standard discovery) — returns contact or company data only, no verified emails

Which would you prefer?"

Only proceed after the user chooses. For company-first campaign prompts such as "marketing agencies in Phoenix" or "Series B fintechs", choose the lane by intent, not by the word "campaign": use Find Companies first, then pass returned company_domains to generate_leads after approval. Use generate_leads when the user explicitly needs verified emails.

BEFORE RUNNING: Tell the user the estimated credit cost based on max_leads and ask for confirmation.

SEARCH PARAMETERS (all optional, AI parses from prompt):
- contact_job_title: Job titles to include (e.g. ["CEO", "CTO"])
- contact_not_job_title: Job titles to exclude
- seniority_level: "founder","owner","c_suite","director","partner","vp","head","manager","senior","entry","trainee"
- functional_level: "c_suite","finance","product_management","engineering","design","education","human_resources","information_technology","legal","marketing","operations","sales","support"
- contact_location: Region/country/state lowercase (e.g. ["united states","california, us"])
- contact_city: City-level targeting (e.g. ["austin","san francisco"])
- contact_not_location / contact_not_city: Exclusion filters
- email_status: "validated","not_validated","unknown" (default: ["validated"])
- company_domain: Specific domains (e.g. ["google.com"])
- size: Employee count buckets: "0-1","2-10","11-20","21-50","51-100","101-200","201-500","501-1000","1001-2000","2001-5000","10000+"
- company_industry / company_not_industry: Industry filters
- company_keywords / company_not_keywords: Keyword filters
- min_revenue / max_revenue: Revenue bands: "100K","500K","1M","5M","10M","25M","50M","100M","500M","1B","5B","10B"
- funding: "Seed","Angel","Series A","Series B","Series C","Series D","Series E","Series F","Venture","Debt","Convertible","PE","Other"

⚠️ TARGETING SPECIFIC COMPANIES — When the user wants leads at a SPECIFIC SET of companies (e.g. "find CEOs at acme.com, foo.com, bar.com" or "VPs at Stripe and Plaid"), you MUST pass the list via the dedicated "company_domains" parameter. Do NOT rely on the prompt-parser to pick them up — pass them explicitly. Use root domains only (acme.com, not www.acme.com/about).

Submit a job and get a job_id back immediately — poll check_job_status for results.

prompt.description: Natural language description of leads. Be specific about titles, industries, company sizes, locations.

company_domains.description: PREFERRED when targeting a specific set of companies. Pass root domains (e.g. ["stripe.com","plaid.com"]) to restrict the search to those companies only. Use this whenever the user names specific companies — never embed them only in the prompt text.

verify_emails.description: Verify emails for each lead (default: true). Set false for faster results.

file_name.description: Custom label for this run (e.g. "Q2 SaaS Outreach")

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: generate_local_leads
tools.title: Generate Local Leads
tools.description:
[BETA] Find local businesses and their VERIFIED contact emails via Google Maps. Best for small/local businesses, brick-and-mortar, service providers, restaurants, clinics, contractors, agencies.

The `target_verified` parameter is the number of verified, deliverable, non-catch-all leads to return — NOT the number of places searched. Signaliz will continue scraping additional businesses in the area until the target is met or the safety cap (5× target, max 5,000) is reached.

Returns business data (name, address, phone, website, ratings, reviews) plus verified emails only. Catch-all, unverifiable, placeholder, and malformed emails are filtered out before return.

BEFORE RUNNING: Tell the user the estimated credit cost (1 credit per verified email returned; the safety cap means worst-case credit cost is bounded at target_verified × 1, not 5×) and ask for confirmation. Submit a job and get a job_id back immediately — poll check_job_status for results.

prompt.description: Business type + location, e.g. 'lawyers in Phoenix, AZ'

target_verified.description: Verified leads to return (default: 100). NOT places searched — Signaliz auto-continues until target met or area exhausted.

max_leads.description: [DEPRECATED] Use target_verified instead. Kept for backward compatibility.

verify_emails.description: Verify emails for each lead (default: true). Set false for faster results.

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: create_routine
tools.title: Create Routine
tools.description:
🎯 Create a goal-driven Ops Routine (autonomous agent).

The agent works on the goal autonomously on a schedule (hourly/daily/weekly) or on-demand (manual), respecting policy guardrails and writing results to configured output sinks.

EXAMPLES OF GOALS:
- "Find 50 new fintech CTOs in NYC each week and add them to our outreach list"
- "Monitor our top 100 target accounts daily for hiring signals and push to Slack"
- "Every morning, qualify the leads in 'New Inbound' against our ICP and route to sales"

OUTPUT SINKS (where results land each tick):
- { type: 'csv' } — append to a workspace CSV (download via signed URL)
- { type: 'webhook', config: { url: '...' } } — POST results to your endpoint

After creating, set status='active' (or use update_routine) to start ticking.

goal.description: Plain-English goal the agent works toward each tick

description.description: Optional context: ICP details, exclusions, success criteria

cadence.description: How often the routine ticks. Use "manual" for agent-driven routines that only run via run_routine_now.

status.description: Initial status. Set to "active" to start ticking immediately.

enabled.description: Whether this sink is active (default: true)

output_sinks.description: Where each tick writes its results

wake_on_events.description: Event names that trigger an out-of-schedule tick (e.g. ["lead.new", "signal.detected"])

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: list_routines
tools.title: List Routines
tools.description: List all Ops Routines in the workspace. Shows name, status, cadence, last/next tick, and routine ID.

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: get_routine
tools.title: Get Routine
tools.description: Get full details of an Ops Routine including goal, policy, sinks, recent ticks, and 30-day outcomes.

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: update_routine
tools.title: Update Routine
tools.description: Update an Ops Routine's configuration. Change name, goal, cadence, output sinks, policy guardrails, or status. Setting status='active' activates a draft/paused routine; status='paused' stops scheduled ticks (manual run_routine_now still works).

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: run_routine_now
tools.title: Run Routine Now
tools.description: Manually trigger an Ops Routine to tick immediately, bypassing its schedule. Returns a run_id you can use to track the tick. Optional 'instruction' lets you steer this specific run (e.g. "focus on EU companies this time"); the routine's permanent goal is unchanged.

routine_id.description: ID of the routine to trigger

instruction.description: Optional one-off instruction to steer this tick

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: delete_routine
tools.title: Delete Routine
tools.description: Delete an Ops Routine. By default this is a soft-delete (archives the routine and stops further ticks; historical ticks/items are preserved). Pass permanent=true to hard-delete the routine and cascade-delete all its ticks and items. Requires confirm=true.

confirm.description: Must be true to confirm deletion

permanent.description: If true, hard-delete (cascade ticks/items). Default: false (soft-archive).

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: get_routine_ticks
tools.title: Get Routine Ticks
tools.description: List historical ticks for an Ops Routine — when it ran, status (queued/running/completed/failed), records produced, credits used, and any error message. Use 'before' for pagination. To fetch actual rows produced by a tick, call get_tick_items(tick_id) or get_last_tick_items(routine_id).

before.description: ISO timestamp — return ticks started before this (for pagination)

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: get_tick_items
tools.title: Get Tick Items
tools.description: Fetch the actual records produced by a single Ops Routine tick. Returns rows from gtm_routine_items (item_data jsonb + subject_key + state) for the given tick_id. Paginate with 'cursor' (ISO created_at) and 'limit' (max 500).

state.description: Optional filter: only items with this state

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: get_last_tick_items
tools.title: Get Last Tick Items
tools.description: Convenience: fetch the records produced by the most recent successful tick of an Ops Routine, in one call. Equivalent to get_routine_ticks(routine_id, limit=1) → get_tick_items(latest_tick_id). This is the 80% case for "show me what this routine just produced". Paginate with 'cursor' + 'limit' (max 500).

state.description: Optional filter: only items with this state

include_failed_ticks.description: If true, also consider failed/partial ticks. Default: false.

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: get_routine_results
tools.title: Get Routine Results
tools.description:
🤖 AGENT CONVENIENCE: Get the latest results from an Ops Routine as structured JSON.

Combines get_routine + get_last_tick_items into one call. Returns routine metadata, tick info, and all produced items in a single response. Perfect for agent consumption — always returns JSON regardless of output_format setting.

Use this when you need to:
- Check what an Op just produced
- Pull results into your agent's context for further processing
- Chain Op outputs into another tool call

routine_id.description: ID of the routine to get results from

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: agent_workflow
tools.title: Agent Workflow
tools.description:
🤖 AGENT ORCHESTRATION: Create, trigger, and optionally wait for an Ops Routine in a single call.

This is the primary tool for agents that want to spin up an autonomous Op, run it, and get results back.

Workflow:
1. Creates a manual-cadence Ops Routine with your goal and config
2. Activates it and triggers an immediate tick
3. If wait=true (default), polls until the tick completes and returns results
4. If wait=false, returns the routine_id and run_id for you to poll later

EXAMPLES:
- { goal: "Find 50 SaaS founders in Austin TX", name: "Austin SaaS Discovery", output_sinks: [{type: "csv"}] }
- { goal: "Enrich these companies with hiring signals", name: "Company Enrichment", instruction: "Focus on Series A-C companies" }
- { goal: "Score these leads against our ICP", name: "ICP Scoring", wait: false }

name.description: Human-readable name for this workflow run

goal.description: Plain-English goal for the agent to accomplish

description.description: Additional context: ICP details, exclusions, success criteria

instruction.description: One-off instruction to steer the first tick

wake_on_events.description: Event types to subscribe to for future triggers

wait.description: If true (default), poll until the tick completes and return results. If false, return immediately with routine_id and run_id.

max_wait_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait for tick completion (default: 300 = 5 min)

cleanup.description: If true, delete the routine after retrieving results (for one-shot workflows)

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: emit_event
tools.title: Emit Event
tools.description: Fire an event that wakes any active Op subscribed to that event type (via its wake_on_events list). Example use cases: pipe Crunchbase funding notifications, LinkedIn job change webhooks, intent signals from Bombora, or custom events from Zapier. Include a dedup_key if you expect the same external event might be delivered twice — identical (workspace_id, dedup_key) pairs are no-oped.

subject_key.description: Identifier of the subject (email, domain, company_id)

metadata.description: Event payload — passed to the routine as context

output_format.description: Response format. Use 'json' for programmatic/agent consumption.

tools.name: approvals_list
